usage: Use as an optional cold-open language for Chinese talking-head or interview videos. Adapt copy, accents, timing and composition to the episode; do not apply it as continuous body captions.

typography.policy: Keep a strong size hierarchy between hero words, supporting phrases and annotations. Adjust for glyph width, face position and available negative space.

color.accentPolicy: Choose one or two semantic accents from the episode color direction. Prefer non-green type accents and do not inherit the source case yellow or green automatically.

composition.preferredPlacement: negative space beside or below the person

motion.ordinaryWords: appear crisp at the spoken beat

focus.intent: fast focus acquisition with a soft uninterrupted tail

editing.camera: static crops chosen at cut points
editing.broll: use real evidence full-screen when it carries the sentence; prepare seek-safe proxies when source GOPs are sparse

useWhen: a short spoken hook has one or two words whose meaning benefits from being visually brought into focus
the person and real setting should remain the visual anchor
the opening needs impact without looking like a poster or effects reel
avoidWhen: every sentence would need the same focus treatment
the copy is long enough to behave like body captions
the focus effect would cover a face, mouth or evidence
the episode tone calls for restrained documentary typography with no visible effect
